title: Phone line acceptance (17f): the operator calls in, an AI-voice Richard screens and presents
note: Times are seconds from the start the runner prints (T0). The operator follows the 'operator' cues on the runner's screen and never needs to hear the phone: every question Richard asks is shown as text at the moment he asks it. 'richard' lines are spoken by the harness in the AI voice; 'act' lines are the harness's studio actions through the control plane's API. 'check' says what the observer confirms afterwards from the recordings and logs.

routes.trunk: Dial the station's number from the phone's dialler. The station plays the consent words (or none, with them off); press any key when they end.
routes.browser: Open the station's player page in the phone's browser (the G0 way: Jelly on LineageOS, driven over adb and CDP), tap Call in, type a name and a line, tick the consent box and call.

cues.text: Ring in now. Trunk: dial the number. Browser: tap Call in, fill the form, tick the box, Call.
cues.check: trunk: the words are heard in full on the caller's recording (Whisper matches the words' text); the caller is in no queue and no mix before the key

cues.text: When the words end, press 5 on the keypad (any key carries on).
cues.check: the key arrives as an RFC 4733 event; a consent record with given_by caller, line phone, the words' version and no number

cues.text: Wait. You are in the queue now.
cues.check: the screener's card shows Phone ···NNNN (trunk) or the typed name (browser); no name from LiveKit

cues.text: The screener picks the caller up (T).

cues.say: Hello, you're through to the studio. Can I take your first name?

cues.prompt: Hello, you're through to the studio. Can I take your first name?
cues.text: Say a first name (Morag will do).

cues.say: Lovely. And what would you like to talk about tonight?

cues.prompt: And what would you like to talk about tonight?
cues.text: Say one or two sentences: a topic of your choice.

cues.say: Thanks. For a line check, please count from one to five.

cues.text: Count one, two, three, four, five, about one a second.
cues.check: Whisper on the screener's ear finds one to five; the return to the caller was heard (getStats on the browser route; the phone's own ear on the trunk route)

cues.say: Now stay silent for ten seconds, please, while I check the line.

cues.check: the caller's level is below the gate for these ten seconds; no noise bursts in the programme

cues.say: Thank you. I'm putting you through to the presenter now. Stay on the line.

cues.text: The screener sends the caller to the desk (P).
The presenter puts the caller on air.

cues.say: And we have a caller on the line. You're on air: tell us who you are and where you're calling from.

cues.prompt: You're on air: tell us who you are and where you're calling from.
cues.text: Say your name and a town.
cues.check: the caller's voice is in the listener stream about the listener delay later; the phone hears Richard (return) and not themselves (mix-minus)

cues.say: What's the strangest thing you've seen this week?

cues.prompt: What's the strangest thing you've seen this week?

cues.say: Now keep talking while I talk over you, so we can hear how the line copes with two voices at once.

cues.prompt: Keep talking while Richard talks over you.
cues.text: Talk for ten seconds without stopping.

cues.say: I'm talking over our caller on purpose, reading a long sentence, so that both voices are on the line together for a few seconds.
Lovely. Count down from five for us, slowly.

cues.check: no echo of the caller in their own return; both voices clear in the programme during the overlap

cues.say: Thank you so much for calling the studio. Goodbye for now.

cues.text: Stay on the line and say nothing. The studio ends the call.
cues.check: the call ends from the studio's side (drop); the phone shows the call ended within a few seconds

cues.text: The screener drops the caller (Ctrl+D Ctrl+D).
Done. Note anything you heard that was wrong.
